content:
Tomislav Mesarić
Ulica Lipa 12, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia | +385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com

PROFESSIONAL PROFILE
Butcher with 9 years of experience in high-street and market meat counters, supported by completed vocational butcher training and HACCP basic food hygiene certification. Experienced in breaking down beef, pork and lamb, boning and trimming, portioning orders, making fresh sausages, advising customers on cuts and cooking, and maintaining temperature and hygiene records. Familiar with FIFO stock rotation and training apprentices.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante (family butcher shop), Zagreb | 2019–Present
- Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides per week; bone, trim and portion meat for the counter.
- Make four kinds of fresh sausage to the shop’s recipes: ćevapi, kobasice, chipolata and lamb merguez; produce about 40 kg weekly in the busy season.
- Developed the shop’s lamb merguez recipe and adjusted the ćevapi mix to 70% beef and 30% lamb following customer feedback. The ćevapi won second place at the 2023 Zagreb County craft meat fair.
- Maintain cold-room and display-counter temperature records, checking twice daily; rotate cold-room stock every morning using FIFO, with older stock at the front.
- Serve about 120 customers on a Saturday, advising on cuts and cooking times.
- Train two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.
- Prepare whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting orders, including ordering, butchering, seasoning and delivery. This has included catering for weddings and family parties; the largest order was four lambs and two pigs for a 180-guest wedding in 2024.
- Ran a six-week dry-ageing trial on beef ribs, keeping weight-loss and temperature records. Dry-aged rib is now sold by pre-order, at about 15 kg per month.

Counter Assistant | Tržnica Dolac meat hall stall, Zagreb | 2015–2019
- Served customers, weighed and priced orders, operated the till and completed cash-up.
- Cleaned and sanitised slicers, mincers and the counter at closing.
- Wrote a one-page closing and cleaning checklist after a hygiene inspection remark; it remains in use at the stall.

EDUCATION & CERTIFICATES
Vocational Certificate: Butcher (3-year programme) | Food Trades School Zagreb | 2015
HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate | 2021; renewed 2024
Preparing for the master butcher exam (majstorski ispit), planned for spring 2027; not yet passed.

SKILLS
Carcass breakdown (beef, pork and lamb) · Boning and trimming · Portioning meat to order · Fresh sausage making · Knife sharpening · Mincer and bandsaw operation · FIFO stock rotation · Cold-chain temperature and hygiene checks · Customer service and product advice · Cash handling · Cleaning and sanitising equipment · Hand pallet jack

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) · English (good; customer service) · German (basic)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, clear and highly relevant CV. It presents nine years of directly relevant butchery and meat-counter experience, quantified production and customer volumes, practical HACCP-related duties, customer advice, FIFO rotation and apprentice training. The added project-level achievements—sausage development, the award, catering orders and dry-ageing trial—give the CV considerably more impact than a basic duties-only CV. The structure is logical and easy to scan. The only substantive content concern is a potentially overbroad statement about maintaining “hygiene records”; the original candidate information explicitly supports temperature records and hygiene/cleaning procedures, but does not clearly confirm formal hygiene records.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional section headings, standard reverse-chronological experience, readable bullet points and relevant searchable terms such as butcher, HACCP, boning, trimming, portioning, sausage making, FIFO, temperature records, customer service and cash handling. It should have a high ATS screening probability for the stated must-have requirements. The terminology also aligns well with the advert’s wording, including “counter,” “portion,” “advise customers,” “FIFO,” and “temperature.” No problematic tables, graphics, columns or unusual formatting are present. For maximum keyword alignment, “package” or “paper-wrap customer orders” could be included only if desired and only as a factual description of the candidate’s existing practice; the CV should not imply experience with tray sealers, labelling scales or self-service supermarket packing.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is excellent for the core role. The CV clearly shows completed butcher training, substantially more than two years at a meat counter, HACCP knowledge, cutting and portioning, customer advice, FIFO stock rotation, temperature checks and cleaning/sanitation. These directly match FreshCart’s service-counter duties and its emphasis on reliability, hygiene, friendliness, product knowledge and practical experience. The customer volume, Saturday experience and apprentice training also support the retail environment. The candidate’s material shows no forklift licence, so that nice-to-have is a gap rather than a CV defect. The candidate also has no supermarket experience and has not used tray sealers or self-service labelling scales; these are experience gaps, although the existing counter and paper-wrapping experience remain relevant. The Wednesday early-shift constraint noted in the candidate material may need consideration against the employer’s alternating schedule, but it is not a defect in this CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Profile, change “maintaining temperature and hygiene records” to the more precisely supported wording “maintaining temperature records and following hygiene and cleaning procedures.” This avoids implying formal hygiene-record documentation that is not clearly stated in the Original Candidate Information.

MINOR — In the Skills section, consider changing “Cold-chain temperature and hygiene checks” to “Cold-chain temperature checks and hygiene procedures” for the same precision and consistency with the documented experience.
critique.critical_issues:
Potential truthfulness issue: the Professional Profile states that the candidate maintains “hygiene records,” but the Original Candidate Information explicitly confirms temperature logs, cleaning routines and a cleaning checklist—not formal hygiene records. This must be narrowed to avoid overstating documented experience. The corresponding Skills wording also presents “hygiene checks” more broadly than the source material clearly supports.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “maintaining temperature and hygiene records”
- “Cold-chain temperature and hygiene checks”

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear headings, reverse-chronological experience, relevant vocational training, and concrete evidence of butchery, customer service, hygiene, stock rotation, and training experience. The quantified achievements—weekly carcass volumes, customer numbers, sausage production, and the 180-guest catering order—make the experience credible and impactful. The content is professional and substantially more complete than the original candidate CV. The master butcher exam is correctly described as preparation only, avoiding overstatement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional headings, plain text formatting, standard date ranges, and relevant terms such as butcher, meat counter, HACCP, FIFO, temperature records, boning, trimming, portioning, customer service, and cleaning and sanitising. It should have a high probability of passing initial ATS and AI screening for this role because the two principal requirements are explicit and repeated naturally. The document does not claim unsupported supermarket, tray-sealing, self-service packaging, or forklift experience. For a small ATS improvement, the exact phrase “HACCP knowledge” and the job’s phrase “cut, portion and package” could be incorporated only to the extent supported by the candidate’s experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is excellent. The CV clearly demonstrates completed butcher training, nine years of meat-counter experience, HACCP knowledge, carcass breakdown, portioning, customer advice, FIFO stock rotation, temperature checks, hygiene routines, and equipment cleaning. It also reflects FreshCart’s stated values of reliability, hygiene, friendliness, product knowledge, and pride in good work through evidence such as customer advice, apprentice training, the cleaning checklist, and recipe development. The candidate has no forklift licence, which is a nice-to-have rather than a required qualification; this is a candidate gap, not a CV defect. The CV also does not show supermarket self-service packaging or tray-sealer experience, but the candidate’s material confirms that this experience is not held, so it should not be implied.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS ENHANCEMENT — In the SKILLS section, change “Cold-chain temperature checks and hygiene procedures” to “HACCP knowledge; cold-chain temperature checks; hygiene and cleaning procedures” so the ad’s exact HACCP terminology is more prominent.

MINOR ALIGNMENT ENHANCEMENT — In the Professional Profile, change “portioning orders” to “cutting, portioning and wrapping meat orders” because the candidate’s notes confirm experience wrapping meat in paper. Do not imply experience with tray sealers, labelling scales, or self-service packaging.

MINOR KEYWORD ENHANCEMENT — In the Butcher role at Mesnica Kod Ante, revise “bone, trim and portion meat for the counter” to “cut, bone, trim and portion fresh meat for the service counter.” This more closely matches the advertisement’s language while remaining supported by the candidate’s experience.
